# Frequency Analysis

```{r, setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(magrittr)
library(driveanalytics)

knitr::opts_knit$set(echo = FALSE)

# Get the render format
render_format <- knitr::opts_knit$get('rmarkdown.pandoc.to')
if (render_format == "") render_format <- "html"
```


## Overview
This method calculates and presents the frequency of input events, by cohort.
The primary use for this module is to explore the most common events in each cohort and comparing between them.

There are two metrics calculated in the analysis, based on an input data set and patient cohort.

1. Total count of the number of subjects who have ever had each event, per cohort
1. Frequency (subjects per number in cohort) of each event type, per cohort

This analysis produces three outputs

1. A bar plot of the top N events, in order of descending frequency.
1. A table containing count and frequency values for all event types.

## Method
Event counts are calculated by summing the number of patients who have ever had each event type.

Event frequencies are calculated by dividing the counts by the sizes of each input cohort.

## Considerations and Limitations
* If a subject has the same event multiple times, this only counts once. Therefore, no individual event can have a frequency higher than 100%.

## Example
The following frequency analysis plot and results table are from a randomly generated set of 500 events across 100 subjects.


This frequency analysis example shows the following information:

1. The most common event in cohort A is *Event W*, with 33.33 % of the cohort having had it during the period under consideration.
1. Comparatively, only 16.28 % of cohort B had this event.
1. The most common event in cohort B is *Event O*, with 27.91 % of the cohort having had it during the period under consideration.
1. Cohort A had a total of 257 different event types, averaging 4.5 events per subject.
1. Cohort B had a total of 205 different event types, averaging 4.8 events per subject.

```{r, example, echo=FALSE, dpi=200, out.width="100%", fig.dim = c(8, 3)}

# Create a random sample of patients in two cohorts and assign random events
set.seed(123)
n <- 100
nev <- n * 5
df_pde <- tibble::tibble(
  project_id = 1:n,
  cohort_id = project_id,
  cohort = sample(c("A","B"), n, replace = TRUE),
)
df_dia <- df_pde %>%
  dplyr::sample_n(nev, replace = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = sample(paste0("Event ", LETTERS), nev, replace = TRUE))

# Perform frequency analysis and get results
gfa <- driveanalytics::gen_frequency_analysis(df_dia, df_pde, "event", "cohort")
gfa_head <- head(gfa, 26)
plot(gfa_head)
tabulate(gfa_head, render_format)

```
